title: Shakespeare plays for NLP: 91K Tagged Lines
subtitle: Per-line dialogue from all 37 plays — Folger edition, ready for tokenizer training, speaker classification, and LM demos
description: See README.md inside the dataset for full details.

resources.description:
**91,509 spoken lines** from all 37 of Shakespeare's plays — one row per line. UTF-8 encoded, ~8.9 MB. Folger Shakespeare edition (CC BY-NC 3.0).

**Schema**

| Column | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `play` | str | Play slug, e.g. `hamlet`, `romeo-and-juliet` |
| `play_title` | str | Display title, e.g. `Hamlet`, `Romeo and Juliet` |
| `act` | int | Act number (1–5) |
| `scene` | int | Scene number within the act |
| `player` | str | Speaker in UPPERCASE, e.g. `HAMLET`, `LADY MACBETH` |
| `line_number` | str | Folger reference `act.scene.line` (e.g. `1.1.2`). Empty for partial / shared lines that don't anchor a full verse line. |
| `line_text` | str | Spoken text. Stage directions removed; Folger smart punctuation preserved. |

**Quick start**

```python
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('shakespeare_lines.csv')

# pull a single scene
df[(df.play == 'hamlet') & (df.act == 3) & (df.scene == 1)]

# top 10 most prolific speakers
df['player'].value_counts().head(10)

# all of Hamlet's lines as one string
'\n'.join(df[df.player == 'HAMLET']['line_text'])
```

**Heads-up**

- **Row order matters** within `(play, act, scene)` — preserved from the source, so sequence-style use cases work even when `line_number` is empty.
- **Speaker labels are raw:** `KING`, `KING HENRY`, `KING HENRY V` are distinct values across plays. Normalize if you need a single canonical character identity. (956 unique labels in total.)
- **No `<unk>` / missing-data sentinels** — empty `player` (50 rows) and empty `line_number` (~11K rows) come through as standard NaN.
